stem: A client asks how an excisional biopsy differs from a core needle biopsy. Which explanation by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: An excisional biopsy surgically removes the entire lump or suspicious area for pathologic examination, whereas a core needle biopsy removes a tissue sample with a wide needle.
options.B: An excisional biopsy and a core needle biopsy both remove only a small portion of the lesion, but they use different anesthetic medications.
options.C: A core needle biopsy removes the entire suspicious lesion, whereas an excisional biopsy removes only a narrow tissue cylinder.
options.D: An excisional biopsy establishes that no further cancer surgery can ever be needed because removal of the visible lesion is always definitive treatment.

rationale: NCI defines excisional biopsy as surgical removal of an entire lump or suspicious area so that it can be examined for disease; a small amount of surrounding normal tissue may also be removed. A core needle biopsy uses a wide needle to remove a tissue sample rather than the entire lesion. Although excision may remove all visible abnormal tissue in some situations, a diagnostic excisional biopsy should not be represented as automatically definitive cancer treatment because subsequent management depends on pathology, margins, cancer type, stage, and other clinical factors.
educational_objective: Differentiate excisional biopsy from core needle biopsy by the amount and method of tissue obtained without confusing diagnostic excision with guaranteed definitive treatment.

correction_summary: Rebuilt the original comparison item using direct NCI definitions and removed the overbroad claim that an excisional biopsy inherently provides therapeutic benefit. The final version precisely distinguishes complete surgical removal of the suspicious area for diagnostic examination from wide-needle tissue sampling and explicitly prevents the inference that diagnostic excision always eliminates the need for further treatment.
audit_findings: Original answer correctly distinguished whole-lesion removal from needle sampling but added a potentially misleading therapeutic implication.
Fresh NCI verification directly defines excisional biopsy as removal of the entire suspicious area and core needle biopsy as wide-needle tissue sampling.
The final question avoids implying that removal of the visible lesion guarantees adequate cancer margins or eliminates later surgery.
Distractors test reversal of procedure definitions and a realistic diagnostic-versus-definitive-treatment misconception.
Independent adversarial review found one uniquely correct explanation with no ambiguity, second answer, cueing, unsupported treatment claim, or unresolved source conflict.
